text:
maria: Hey team — customer reports a sudden spike of 429s followed by 500s when hitting /v1/generate in eu-west1. They say it started after a traffic burst. Have request IDs and a small log excerpt. Can we get repro snippets to share?

kevin: Thanks — can you paste one of the request IDs and the exact timestamp? Also which model variant and client (curl/sdk/js)?

maria: Request IDs: x-req-12345, x-req-12346. Timestamps: 2026-03-16T15:02:12Z and 2026-03-16T15:02:14Z. Using our internal JS client + some curl traffic from their load generator. Model: gptx-medium-2048. Region: eu-west1.

jun: Quick repro snippets below — share these with customer so we can reproduce quickly. Keep concurrency small first, then scale up.

maria: paste away pls

jun: Minimal curl to hit the same endpoint with request id header (single threaded):

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\ 
  -H "X-Request-ID: repro-curl-$(date +%s)" \\ 
  -d '{"model":"gptx-medium-2048","input":"hello world","max_tokens":16}'
```

jun: Minimal Python (requests) single request:

```python
import os
import requests

url = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
headers = {
    "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY']}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "X-Request-ID": "repro-py-1"
}
json = {"model":"gptx-medium-2048","input":"test","max_tokens":16}
resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=json, timeout=15)
print(resp.status_code, resp.headers.get('x-request-id'))
print(resp.text)
```

jun: Node fetch example:

```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate';
(async () => {
  const res = await fetch(url, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_KEY}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      'X-Request-ID': 'repro-js-1'
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({model:'gptx-medium-2048', input:'hi', max_tokens:16})
  });
  console.log(res.status, res.headers.get('x-request-id'));
  console.log(await res.text());
})();
```

jun: Go tiny stress test (concurrent):

```go
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "net/http"
  "os"
  "sync"
)
func main() {
  client := &http.Client{}
  var wg sync.WaitGroup
  for i:=0;i<50;i++ {
    wg.Add(1)
    go func(i int){
      defer wg.Done()
      req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", bytes.NewBufferString(`{"model":"gptx-medium-2048","input":"burst test","max_tokens":8}`))
      req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
      req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
      req.Header.Set("X-Request-ID", fmt.Sprintf("repro-go-%d", i))
      res, err := client.Do(req)
      if err!=nil { fmt.Println("err", err); return }
      fmt.Println("status", res.StatusCode, "id", res.Header.Get("x-request-id"))
      res.Body.Close()
    }(i)
  }
  wg.Wait()
}
```

maria: perfect. also need guidance on what logs/debug bundle to collect from customer.

kevin: Ask them to collect: request IDs, client-side timings (DNS/connect/TLS/request/ttfb), and a tcpdump/pcap if they can (100KB slice around the event). On our side we need server logs for those request IDs and the backend error traces.

kevin: For quick debug bundle we have the support-bundle helper: `curl https://support.redwood.ai/bundle.sh | bash` — this collects environment, SDK versions, and network info. Ask them to run with `--short` to keep size small.

sre-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-322. Attach logs with a matching tag `inc-2026-322`.

eng-qa: A few tips when reproducing:
- Start single request, confirm 200.
- Increase concurrency by factors (2,5,10) until you hit 429.
- If 500s follow, capture full response bodies and relay them (do not redact error IDs).
- Try both with and without client-side retries/backoff — retries can magnify burst behavior.

maria: I'll send the snippets + bundle instructions to the customer and ask them to run the Go stress test with `-concurrency 50` and share the output and the support bundle.

kevin: If they can reproduce, include one raw 500 response body and the corresponding X-Request-ID header. We'll pull traces. Also note whether they were routing via a proxy or using NAT'd IPs — e.g., cloud load generator can hit per-IP token buckets.

maria: sending now. Thanks all :thumbsup:
